source.title: Trump-Xi summit: What wasn't said might matter the most
source.summary: The most revealing thing about the summit in Washington may be what the two leaders did not say - and what we still don't know.
source.evidence_text:
The most revealing thing about the summit in Washington may be what the two leaders did not say - and what we still don't know.
On Monday, China released more information of what was agreed at the talks between Xi Jinping and Donald Tump last week, shedding light on a handful of concrete outcomes.
But there were no joint statements and few major breakthroughs.
Beijing says it has agreed with Washington to launch a new AI dialogue, with further talks scheduled for the end of November.
Chinese state media confirmed for the first time on Monday that the trade truce has been extended until 10 January.
This summit produced more dialogue - but very little decision change for now. The most contentious issues from advanced technology to Taiwan remain unresolved.
Instead, both governments issued separate accounts of the meeting - perhaps a sign that despite the White House tours and promise of warmer ties, Washington and Beijing remain wary of each other.
They have also agreed to establish a communication channel for AI-related incidents, aimed at preventing misunderstandings or unexpected developments from turning into a broader confrontation.
But Beijing had hoped for a much longer extension to the truce, making the two month reprieve a modest gain rather than a major breakthrough.
China did secure lower tariffs on $30bn (£23bn) of goods entering the US with reciprocal reductions expected from Beijing.
There was no mention of increasing exports of China's rare earth minerals to the US nor was there any indication that restrictions on advanced US semiconductors would be eased.
The White House factsheet made no mention of Taiwan, but the issue was clearly a priority for Xi Jinping.
According to Beijing's accounts of the talks, Xi urged Donald Trump to formally oppose Taiwan independence and handle the issue with caution.
Meanwhile the US State Department continues to classify travel to China as a Level 2 advisory urging travellers to "exercise increased caution" because of the risk of arbitrary law enforcement, exit bans and detention.
As both countries race to develop advanced artificial intelligence, the move suggests they see a need for some guardrails around a technology that is increasingly being used in everything from business to military planning.
What is striking is what was left out.
And while both remain committed to a steady relationship - continued US-China dialogue appears far easier than asking either superpower to compromise.

vocabulary.definition: Important or interesting; deserving attention.

grammar.explanation: The present perfect passive is used to describe an action that happened at an unspecified time in the past and has a connection to the present, focusing on the action itself rather than who performed it. It is formed with "has/have been" + the past participle of the main verb. For example, in the sentence "The trade truce has been extended," we know the truce is now longer, but the focus is on the extension, not specifically on who extended it.
grammar.example_quote: Chinese state media confirmed the trade truce has been extended until January 10.

quiz.question: What does the reading suggest was the most significant aspect of the Trump-Xi summit?
options: The clear agreements made on all major issues.
What the leaders chose not to say or discuss openly.
The immediate resolution of all trade disputes.
option_feedback: The article states there were 'few major breakthroughs' and many issues remain 'unresolved', indicating not all issues were clearly agreed upon.
The first sentence of the reading highlights that the summit was 'notable for what was not explicitly said,' implying this was the most important aspect.
The reading notes that a 'trade truce has been extended' and some tariffs were lowered, but it does not say all trade disputes were immediately resolved.

To launch a new dialogue and establish a communication channel for AI-related incidents.

The article explicitly mentions that the countries agreed to 'launch a new dialogue on artificial intelligence' and establish a 'communication channel' to prevent misunderstandings.
The reading does not mention any agreement to share all advanced AI technology; it focuses on communication and dialogue.

option_feedback: The reading suggests separate accounts and unresolved issues, which contradicts excitement or enthusiasm.
The article states that issuing 'separate accounts' suggests they remain 'wary,' implying a lack of full trust.
To be 'wary' means to be cautious and suspicious, which fits the context of countries issuing separate statements despite promises of warmer ties.

It was extended until January 10.
It was replaced by a new, permanent trade agreement.

option_feedback: Tariffs are not about increasing trade volume; they are taxes on trade.
The reading explains that 'China secured lower tariffs on $30bn of goods entering the US,' which refers to taxes on trade, not volume.
While travel advisories are mentioned in the article, tariffs specifically relate to taxes on goods, not travel.

quiz.question: In the sentence, "The trade truce has been extended until January 10," what does the passive voice highlight?
options: That Chinese state media personally extended the truce.

The passive voice 'has been extended' emphasizes the action and its result (the longer truce) rather than specifying the agent who performed the extension.
The sentence does not attribute the extension solely to Trump; the passive voice avoids specific attribution.

The reading states the US State Department continues to classify travel as a Level 2 advisory, urging increased caution due to risks.
The article says the advisory 'continues,' implying previous warnings are still in place and have not been lifted, due to ongoing risks.
